$comment: Spec-as-fixture for issue #74: git-guardrails push-target parsing. Each case is run against BOTH harness copies (extensions/git-guardrails.ts and hooks/block-dangerous-git.sh) — verdicts must match (parity gate). 'branch' = the current branch of the repo the command would act on ('' = not a repo / branch unresolvable). 'cwd_branch' vs 'c_path_branch' distinguish the shell cwd repo from a `git -C <path>` target repo. OPTIONAL WITNESS FIELDS (#260): 'pre74' records what the FROZEN pre-#74 ancestor (tests/fixtures/block-dangerous-git.pre-74.sh) actually returned for this case — measured by research/260-measure-pre74-verdicts.ts, not asserted from memory — and 'pre74_class' names which historical defect it demonstrates: greedy-push-regex, cwd-only-branch, or substring-checkout-dot. A case WITHOUT these fields makes no historical claim. Of 124 cases the ancestor agreed on 79 and differed on 45; only the 24 differences traceable to a defect it had BY ITS OWN STATED INTENT are annotated. The other 21 are rules that did not exist yet (gh pr merge, --all/--mirror/--branches, HEAD/@ and matching refspecs, branch flag clusters, --repo, clean --force) — the ancestor was not wrong about those, it had no opinion, and calling them bugs would overstate the case. Since #301 it also pins the commit-on-main gate (commit/merge/rebase/cherry-pick/am/pull) and the compound-line state: cd/pushd/popd move the effective cwd, checkout -b/switch -c lift the gate for the repo that switched, '( )' groups split like ';'.

cases.command: git push origin feat && gh pr create --base main
cases.why: #74 false-positive class 1: greedy regex spans the && chain; the push targets feat, 'main' belongs to gh pr create
#74 false-positive class 2: \bmain\b matches at the hyphen; ref token must EQUAL main/master, not contain it
#74 false-positive class 3: mere co-occurrence of 'push' and 'main' in a non-git command (hit live 3x)
review finding 6: naive newline/separator split manufactured a 'git push origin main' subcommand out of quoted printf text
a ; inside double quotes is data, not a command separator

cases.command: git commit -m "see: git push origin main"
cases.why: quoted commit message stays one token; the git subcommand is commit
inverse fix: quote chars previously stuck to the token ('"main"' != 'main') so a quoted ref slipped the destination check

cases.command: git push origin feat & git push origin main
cases.why: single & (background) is a command separator too; the second command pushes main

cases.command:
cat > /tmp/notes.md <<'EOF'
git push origin main is blocked by the ruleset
EOF
cases.why: #74 false-positive class 3: heredoc body text is not a git invocation

cases.command:
cat <<-EOF
	indented body
	EOF
git push origin main
cases.why: review finding 7: <<- allows a tab-indented terminator; comparing the raw line to the delimiter never matched, so the REAL push after the heredoc was stripped from inspection

cases.command:
cat <<-EOF
	git push origin main
	EOF
cases.why: tab-indented body of a <<- heredoc is still data; terminator must now be recognized so nothing AFTER leaks, but the body itself never blocks

cases.command:
cat <<EOF
	EOF
git push origin main
EOF
cases.why: without the dash, a tab-indented EOF is NOT a terminator in real shells — the push line is heredoc data, matching bash semantics
review finding 13a: '<<EOF' inside single quotes is data — the blind regex entered body mode and stripped the REAL push on the next line (fail-open)
review finding 13b: heredoc delimiters are general shell WORDs — the identifier-only charset left <<123 unstripped, so body text falsely blocked

cases.command:
cat <<my-delim.1
git push origin main
my-delim.1
cases.why: dashes and dots are valid in heredoc delimiters too
guard on the guard: << inside $(( )) is a bit-shift — treating it as a heredoc opener would strip the real push that follows (the numeric-delimiter fix must not introduce this)
-C aware: explicit refspec targets feat; -C repo branch is feat
existing behavior preserved: bare push on a feature branch is fine
options before the refspec must be skipped, not treated as refs
deleting a non-default remote branch is routine cleanup per standards
review finding 5: first-token-must-be-git let shell wrappers carry the identical dangerous push
env wrapper, same bypass
a leading VAR=val assignment also made the first token non-git — same class, no wrapper binary needed
wrapper with option + numeric argument before git
wrapper with duration argument before git
wrapper stripping must not change the verdict for safe pushes
echo is not a wrapper — prefix skipping stops at unknown words so quoted-less text stays text
review finding 14: bash is not a wrapper, so the prefix scan bailed and the -c payload — a full nested command string — was never inspected
sh -c, same bypass
-c inside a short-flag cluster (-lc) still takes the next argument as the command string
eval re-parses its arguments as a shell command
eval with the command as one quoted word
wrapper prefix then shell runner — the two skip mechanisms must compose
nested -c strings recurse: each layer re-splits and re-tokenizes
the nested check inherits the hook cwd, so branch-aware rules still fire inside -c strings
nested inspection must not change the verdict for safe pushes
no -c: a script-file invocation's arguments are data, not a command string ('main' is just an argument)
#105 (finding 16a): a path-based invocation is still git — match by basename, or the exact-string 'git' test bails
relative-path git binary, always-blocked forced clean
#105 (finding 16b): a command substitution EXECUTES its body — the main tokenizer saw 'echo' and bailed while the push ran (the residual documented at findings 14+15)
backtick substitution, same execution semantics
$() still executes inside double quotes
inside single quotes a substitution is literal text — nothing executes
substitution inspection must not change verdicts for safe git commands
review finding 15: exec replaces the shell with the command — it is a pass-through wrapper the prefix scan bailed on

cases.command: exec -a fakename git push origin main
cases.why: exec -a takes a SEPARATE argv[0] argument — same wrapper-arg shape as sudo -u (finding 11)
review finding 4: --repo IS the remote (git's repository argument), so 'main' is a refspec — treating --repo as an opaque option pair let 'main' land in the remote slot unchecked
same hole via the --repo=<repo> single-token form
--repo with a feature refspec stays allowed
--repo with no refspec is a bare push — current-branch fallback must still fire
--all pushes EVERY local branch including main; the bare-push fallback only sees the feature branch, so mode flags must block outright
--mirror force-updates or deletes every remote ref, main included — never safe for an agent
--branches is the modern alias for --all
tags cannot move main; only branch-mode flags are inherently main-touching
review finding 10: ':' is git's MATCHING refspec — pushes every branch existing on both sides, main included; empty dst never equaled 'main' so it sailed past the destination check
'+:' force-updates all matching branches — strictly worse than ':'
':dst' with a NON-empty dst is a delete of that ref — only main/master deletion blocks; empty-dst detection must not overreach

cases.command: sudo -u root git push origin main
cases.why: review finding 11: sudo -u consumes a separate argument; 'root' failed every prefix check and the guard bailed → fail-open (the residual documented at #74 close, now fixed)

cases.command: env -u GIT_DIR git push origin main
cases.why: env -u NAME, same bypass — NAME is not an assignment, wrapper, flag, or number

cases.command: doas -u root git push origin main
cases.why: doas -u user, same shape as sudo

cases.command: sudo -u root git push origin feat
cases.why: wrapper-arg skipping must not change the verdict for safe pushes
review finding 8: HEAD is a symbolic ref — on main it pushes main, but the literal-string dst check saw 'HEAD' != 'main' and the nonempty refspec list skipped the current-branch fallback
HEAD on a feature branch pushes the feature branch — must stay allowed
@ is shorthand for HEAD, same symbolic resolution
explicit main destination wins regardless of the symbolic source
destination ref token equals main
src:dst refspec — DESTINATION is main even though source is feat
force push with explicit main destination
existing behavior preserved: bare push resolves to current branch = main
NEW (#74 under-block, Phase G escape 2026-07-13): hook resolved branch from shell cwd (non-repo, ''), not the -C target on main; only the server ruleset (GH006) stopped it
relative -C must resolve against the TOOL-CALL cwd, not the guard process's own cwd — otherwise the wrong repo (or none) is inspected and a main push slips through
same relative -C resolution, feature branch stays allowed

review finding 9: git resolves each -C relative to the directory established by the previous one — overwriting cpath inspected cwd/sub (nonexistent → '' → not-main) instead of cwd/rel-repo/sub on main
chained -C resolution, feature branch stays allowed
finding 17 (r3591855555): --git-dir selects the affected repo exactly like -C — skipping it fell back to the hook cwd (on feat) and the main push escaped
--git-dir also takes a SEPARATE argument; the old generic -* skip left '/repo/.git' as the subcommand and 'push' invisible
inverse: the targeted repo is on feat even though the hook cwd is on main — --git-dir must win over cwd in BOTH directions

cases.command: sudo --user root git push origin main
cases.why: finding 18 (r3591939370): sudo --user takes a separate argument like -u; only the short form was modeled, so 'root' bailed the scan

cases.command: sudo --user root git push origin feat
cases.why: long-form wrapper-arg skipping must not change the verdict for safe pushes
finding 19 (r3591939373): shell runners must match by basename like git does — /bin/sh bailed the scan and the -c payload went uninspected
wrappers must match by basename too — /usr/bin/env is still env
-C plus explicit main destination; explicit ref wins regardless of branch

cases.command: git fetch && git push origin main
cases.why: separator-split must still inspect EVERY git-push sub-command, not just the first

cases.command: git push origin feat && git push origin main
cases.why: one blocked sub-command blocks the whole command line (fail-safe)
deleting the default branch ref is a main mutation
master treated identically to main throughout
existing rule preserved
review finding 12: -D is documented shorthand for --delete --force — the exact '-D' match let every other spelling of the same force-delete through
split short flags: -d plus -f equals -D
clustered short flags: git parses -df as -d -f
git branch -D deletes EVERY listed branch — the old check only inspected the token immediately after -D, so main as a second target escaped
scope decision: non-force -d refuses unless the branch is fully merged, so nothing unrecoverable is lost (origin/main restores it); only FORCE deletion of main blocks
force-deleting a feature branch is routine cleanup; only main/master targets block
existing rule preserved: feature-branch deletion allowed
existing rule preserved
-C resolution applies to reset --hard too, same under-block shape as push
existing rule preserved: feature branches may hard-reset
always blocked: discards uncommitted work on any branch
review finding 3: literal-space regex missed multi-space/tab separation; tokenizer is whitespace-agnostic
review finding 3: the -- pathspec separator split the dot into its own token past the old regex
same -- separator escape for restore
review finding 3: -f -d as separate tokens evaded the combined -f/-fd patterns
any short-flag cluster containing f is a forced clean
--force long form equals -f
dry run deletes nothing; only forced cleans discard work
inverse fix: the old substring regex ('git checkout \.') false-blocked dotfile pathspecs; only the bare '.' token discards everything
#183: gh pr create is the LLM's PR creation path — allowed
#183: gh pr merge is human-only — must stay blocked
#183: path-based gh invocation still matches by basename

cases.command: echo 'dont run gh pr merge automatically'
cases.why: #183: 'gh pr merge' in a quoted echo is data, not a command
#183: force-deleting a feature branch (not main) is allowed
#183: pushing to a feature branch (refspec not main/master) is allowed
#208/#189: check_gh_command only inspected T[0]; sudo prefix bypassed the human-only merge gate
#208/#189: env is a GIT_WRAPPERS entry — skipped for git, must be skipped for gh too
#208/#189: VAR=val assignment prefix is benign and must not hide the gh merge
#208/#189: wrapper plus its separate-argument option (-n 10) before gh
#208/#189: sudo's arg-consuming long/short options must be consumed before matching gh
#208/#189: nested shell string recursion must still see the wrapped gh merge
#208/#189 inverse: skipping the prefix must not turn every wrapped gh into a block
#208/#189 inverse: only 'pr merge' is gated, not all wrapped gh commands
#208/#105: literal ' inside double quotes opened a bogus single-quote skip that swallowed the $( ) body
#208/#105: apostrophe in double-quoted text must not suppress substitution scanning
#208/#105 inverse: scanning the body must still judge by target — feat is allowed
#208/#105 inverse: a REAL single-quoted region keeps $( ) literal — must stay allowed

#225 gap 2: `worktree remove --force` discards uncommitted/untracked work unconditionally, same class as `clean -f` — previously entirely unguarded (`rg -c worktree hooks/block-dangerous-git.sh` was 0)
#225 gap 2: short-flag spelling of the same force-remove must be caught too
#225 gap 2 implementation step 3: plain `remove` (no force) stays allowed — git's own refusal on a dirty tree is the existing safeguard (#210's reasoning in pr-cleanup)
#225 gap 2 scoping: `worktree add --force` overrides git's "already checked out elsewhere" refusal, not a data-loss guard — only `remove --force` is gated

#225 gap 3 (documented, NOT fixed): the hook only inspects the Bash tool's literal command string. `git-checkpoint`'s body (git add -A; git commit; git push) is invisible to it — the guard never even resolves the branch, since the first token isn't 'git' or 'gh'. This is a load-bearing bypass, not a bug: pr-open and git-checkpoint depend on being opaque script names to run at all. A future 'fix' that tries to peek into script files would break the workflow this fixture exists to protect.
#301: main advances only through PRs; a raw commit on main is the residual after git-checkpoint's own guard (#225)
#301: master is main; amend rewrites a main commit
#301: the rule is branch-scoped, feature branches commit freely
#301: no repo -> no branch -> nothing to protect (git itself will refuse)
#301: -C selects the affected repo (#74 finding 17) - commit into a main repo from a feature cwd is still a commit on main
#301: cwd on main is irrelevant when -C points at a feature repo
#301: 'never merge locally' - a local merge into main is a PR bypass
#301 (Duppy): fast-forwarding local main to origin creates no new commit; explicitly allowed
#301: --abort undoes; blocking it would strand a repo mid-merge
#301: rebase moves main's tip without a PR
#301: --abort undoes
#301: cherry-pick creates a commit on main
#301: am creates commits on main
#301: plain pull = fetch + merge, which can create a merge commit on a diverged main; agents use --ff-only
#301 (Duppy): explicitly allowed - keeps local main current with no new commit
#301: branch-scoped
#301 deadlock condition: the escape from main must always work
#301 deadlock condition: switch -c is the other spelling
#301 compound hard case: the branch is resolved before the line runs, so an earlier checkout -b in the same line must lift the gate for the rest of it
#301: same lift for switch -c, ';' separator

cases.command: git checkout main && git commit -m x
cases.why: #301: the reverse - a plain checkout TO main marks the rest of the line as on main even though the cwd is on a feature branch now
#301 fail-safe: a positional to checkout may be a path (file restore), so a plain checkout <name> never lifts the gate - run it as its own command
#301: the lift is keyed to the repo that switched; the -C repo left main, the cwd repo did not

cases.command:
cat <<'EOF' > notes.md
git commit -m x on main
EOF
cases.why: #301: heredoc bodies are data (#74 class 3) - no git runs
#301: quoted text is not a command
#301: cd moves the effective cwd for the rest of the line - the commit lands in the feature repo, not the main-clone cwd (the 'cd wt &&' habit measured at 10% of bash calls)
#301: cd into a main repo, then commit - cd tracking cuts both ways
#301: '( ... )' groups split like ';' so the leading '(' does not hide the cd and the trailing ')' does not hide the subcommand

cases.command: cd rel-repo && cd - && git commit -m x
cases.why: #301 fail-safe: 'cd -' resets the effective cwd to the tool-call cwd (main) rather than guessing

cases.command: cd rel-repo && git checkout -b 301-slug && git commit -m x
cases.why: #301: cd into a main repo, escape with checkout -b, commit - both pieces of line-state compose
#301: cd tracking also fixes the pre-existing bare-push false block from a main-clone cwd
PR #305 review: a cd inside '( )' never reaches the parent shell — the commit after the group runs in the main-clone cwd
PR #305 review: an unresolvable cd operand is unknown, and unknown never moves the modelled cwd — judged against the real cwd (main)
PR #305 review follow-through: a literal NAME=value earlier in the line resolves, so the common 'WT=…; cd "$WT"' shape is not a false block
assignment PREFIX is a command, not a standalone assignment — must still be checked

cases.command: git checkout -b feat2 && git commit -m x
cases.why: PR #305 review: `checkout -b <existing>` fails and leaves the repo on main, so an existing name must not lift the gate

cases.command: git checkout -B feat2 && git commit -m x
cases.why: -B reset-or-creates and always lands on the branch — the lift is sound
PR #305 review: an unresolvable branch operand never lifts — the literal '$UNSET_BRANCH_301' is not a branch

cases.command: BRANCH=301-x; git checkout -b "$BRANCH" && git commit -m x
cases.why: a literal assignment earlier in the line resolves the operand, so the lift applies
PR #305 review: the lift (a branch switch that happened on disk) is visible inside a nested shell string
PR #305 review: a cd that would fail leaves the real shell where it was — the model only moves to a directory that exists
PR #305 review: '--abort' here is the ARGUMENT of -m, and commit has no --abort anyway
same class: '--ff-only' as the -m argument is a message, not the fast-forward guard
PR #305 review: a cd inside $(…) runs in a child shell — the parent's cwd (main) judges the commit
same: bash -c is a child shell

cases.command: WT=rel-repo; WT=.; cd "$WT"; git commit -m x
cases.why: PR #305 round 2: the LAST assignment is the live one — WT ends as '.', the main clone

cases.command: WT=.; WT=rel-repo; cd "$WT"; git commit -m x
cases.why: same, other direction: the last WT points at the feature repo
PR #305 round 2: a variable set inside '( )' does not exist in the parent — the cd is unresolvable, stays put, commit judged on main
PR #305 round 2: substitutions are inspected before the walk; a lift inside one must not reach a commit that ran BEFORE it — nothing from a child shell carries back

cases.command: false && git checkout -b 301-x; git commit -m x
cases.why: PR #305 round 2: a switch that runs only under a condition is reverted when the chain ends at ';' — the commit is judged on main

cases.command: git checkout -b 301-x && git commit -m y; git push
cases.why: the FIRST sub-command of a chain is unconditional, so its lift survives the ';' — the everyday create-commit-push line

cases.command: cd rel-repo && git commit -m x; git push
cases.why: same for cd at the head of a chain

cases.command: true && cd rel-repo; git commit -m x
cases.why: a cd made under a condition is reverted at ';' (fail-closed: the hook cannot know `true` succeeded)

cases.command: cd rel-repo | cat; git commit -m x
cases.why: PR #305 round 2: a pipeline element runs in a subshell — its cd never reaches the shell
a backgrounded sub-command is a subshell too

cases.command: git checkout -b 301-a && git -C rel-repo checkout -b 301-b && git commit -m x
cases.why: PR #305 round 2: lifts are stored per repo — the second repo's switch must not clobber the first's
PR #305 round 3: `pushd -n` pushes onto the dir stack without changing directory — the commit runs in the main-clone cwd
